req-brueghel-hearing.alt: A woman and child sit among musical instruments, clocks and pictures beside three arched windows.
req-brueghel-hearing.note: One of the five Prado sense panels made by Brueghel and Rubens. Instruments and musical activity fill the room around the figures.
req-brueghel-hearing.reason: Numerous instruments and pictures create density, while the small seated figures make quiet hand actions. The large room and window views are prominent; the mood is not the setting score.

present.N: Instruments, written music, clocks and inset pictures provide secondary clues around the musical encounter.
present.S: The near room, three arched windows and distant view make distinct spatial stages.
present.V: The seated figures actively handle a musical instrument rather than merely posing with resting hands.
present.P: Strings, instrument fittings, furniture and small pictures have controlled, finely separated edges.
present.R: Repeated arched openings and upright instrument necks create a visible rhythm across the room.
present.H: The adult and child are joined by attention and hand contact around the instrument.
present.T: A red hanging drape and deliberately displayed instruments frame the seated encounter.
present.M: Wood, metal strings, upholstery, cloth and polished instrument surfaces receive different local descriptions.

unknown.I: The small child has an indistinct shape behind the shoulder, but an impossible body is not clear enough in this reproduction to assign the criterion.

req-brueghel-smell.alt: A woman and child examine flowers in a garden crowded with blossoms, pots, trees and garden buildings.
req-brueghel-smell.note: The figures occupy a small part of an extensive cultivated garden. Containers, plants and a distant arcade extend the theme through the setting.
req-brueghel-smell.reason: Plants and garden architecture dominate. The figures make a small exchange with flowers, while fine botanical and object details make the view dense without much physical action.

present.N: Flowers, vessels, small animals and garden equipment provide clues beyond the central pose.
present.S: The flower-filled foreground opens into a path and recessed garden architecture.
present.V: The adult raises a flower toward her face and the child reaches toward the flowers.
present.L: Vegetation and garden terrain occupy most of the composition.
present.P: Individual stems, petals, vessels and architectural details are finely separated.
present.R: Recurring flower heads and rows of plants establish a conspicuous garden rhythm.
present.H: The adult and child exchange attention and gestures around a flower.
present.M: Petals, foliage, pottery and cloth receive visibly different local treatment.

unknown.I: The small child's anatomy and any possible wing are not sufficiently clear to distinguish an impossible body from an ordinary figure.

req-brueghel-taste.alt: A woman sits at a laden table beside a serving figure, with food, dead game, vessels and pictures filling the room.
req-brueghel-taste.note: A meal is surrounded by an unusually extensive display of food and game. The opened side of the room leads toward an outdoor view.
req-brueghel-taste.reason: Food and game cover much of the foreground. Serving and eating supply modest depicted action; the large interior and garden opening supply setting.

present.N: The meal, game animals, background pictures and vessels offer separate clues around the central encounter.
present.S: The loaded foreground, table and wall pictures lead into a distinct outdoor opening.
present.V: Hands serve and handle items at the table.
present.P: Feathers, tableware, food and small pictures have fine controlled contours.
present.H: The seated woman and standing attendant visibly exchange attention and objects at the meal.
present.T: The foreground food display and framed table present the encounter as an arranged tableau.
present.M: Feathers, fur, vessels, fruit and table linen receive differentiated surface description.

unknown.I: The standing figure may have hybrid anatomy, but the relevant small details are too uncertain to make this a positive visual assignment.

req-brueghel-touch.alt: A woman and child sit among armour, weapons, sculpture and pictures, with activity visible in the background.
req-brueghel-touch.note: The close bodily contact is surrounded by objects associated with different surfaces and physical actions. The panel is one work within the five-sense series.
req-brueghel-touch.reason: Objects fill the view and background work adds physical activity. The central contact is quiet; literal action remains lower than the amount of potential story.

present.N: Armour, weapons, sculpture and the small background activities provide secondary clues beyond the seated group.
present.S: Foreground objects, the seated group and the distant architectural opening make separate physical stages.
present.V: The adult and child touch and hold one another; background figures also work.
present.P: Metal fittings, armour edges, sculptural contours and pictures are finely separated.
present.H: The adult and child are visibly linked by close touch.
present.T: A hanging canopy and the surrounding display frame the seated group.
present.M: Metal armour, sculpture, cloth and skin have different local surface descriptions.

unknown.I: Any wing or hybrid anatomical detail in the small child is unresolved at the reviewed scale.

req-patinir-massys-temptations.alt: Women approach a dark-robed man before an extensive rocky landscape of trees, water, buildings and smaller incidents.
req-patinir-massys-temptations.note: Patinir and Massys collaborated on this panel. The large foreground encounter sits within an extensive landscape containing further small episodes.
req-patinir-massys-temptations.reason: The foreground figures reach and offer an object, while many smaller incidents occupy the distant setting. Rocks, water and wooded terrain retain substantial pictorial weight.

present.N: Small incidents, buildings, animals and the offered object add clues beyond the main foreground group.
present.D: Pale faces and garments stand out against the dark wooded bank and stormy sky.
present.S: The close group, wooded middle ground, rocky settlement and distant water make distinct spatial stages.
present.V: The women reach and offer an object toward the dark-robed figure.
present.F: A compact group of near-view figures occupies a substantial lower area of the image.
present.L: Recognisable terrain, trees, rocks and water organise most of the view.
present.P: Garment edges, buildings, plants and distant incidents are finely differentiated.
present.H: The foreground encounter is linked by directed gazes and an offered object.
present.M: Robes, foliage, rocks and water are locally differentiated.
present.O: Broad areas of water and sky leave open fields above the near encounter.

unknown.I: Some tiny creatures may be hybrid beings, but their anatomy is not clear enough here to turn a fantastical title or subject into a positive visible assignment.

req-caravaggio-david-borghese.alt: A young man lit against darkness extends a severed head and holds a sword across his body.
req-caravaggio-david-borghese.note: This is the Borghese canvas, not Caravaggio's other David versions. The museum retains two possible date ranges rather than one certain1610 date.
req-caravaggio-david-borghese.reason: The head, sword and extended arm make a compact encounter. This is the aftermath of violence, not an image of the beheading in progress; darkness supplies little depicted setting.

present.N: The sword and severed head provide visible event clues beyond the young man's pose.
present.D: Strong light selects face, torso, cloth and head against deep surrounding darkness.
present.V: The extended arm grips and presents the head.
present.F: The torso and head occupy most of the close foreground.
present.P: Facial edges, fabric folds and the sword are carefully controlled.
present.M: Skin, hair, cloth and metal receive different local treatments.
present.O: A large uninterrupted dark field surrounds the figures.

unknown.B: The reproduction shows modelling but does not reliably separate conspicuous paint strokes from surface condition.
unknown.H: A living figure holds a severed head; this does not provide an unambiguous reciprocal human exchange under this criterion.

req-dore-quixote-library.alt: A seated reader is surrounded by books, armour and a rising swarm of imagined knights, creatures and battles.
req-dore-quixote-library.note: The design was first published in1863. This faithful scan comes from a later1906 edition; Doré's design and Pisan's engraving roles are kept separate.
req-dore-quixote-library.reason: Fine engraved marks build a dense room and a swirl of figures. The imagery includes visible combat and physically uncanny creatures, while the reproduction is monochrome.

present.N: Books, armour, a reader and many separate imagined incidents offer numerous event clues.
present.I: A swarm of uncanny creatures and miniature battles appears within and above the ordinary room.
present.D: Large dark hatched areas surround selected light passages around the reader and rising figures.
present.S: The reader, shelves, room and rising imagined incidents occupy several distinct stages.
present.V: The surrounding small figures strike, reach and fight.
present.F: The seated reader is a large near-view human figure.
present.P: Fine engraving differentiates faces, armour, books and many small objects.
present.R: Repeated lances, limbs and curved directions form a rising visual rhythm.
present.H: The miniature combatants visibly confront and act upon one another.
present.T: Curtain-like framing and the arranged central reader stage the encounter.
present.M: Armour, cloth, furniture and book pages receive different engraved descriptions.

req-birkhauser-worlds-wound.alt: A man in a hat looks out from beside a broad vertical partition, with one side of his face strongly lit.
req-birkhauser-worlds-wound.note: The foundation reproduces this image as Der Gespaltene. The Jung Center's slide archive explicitly connects the same composition with the alternate title The World's Wound.
req-birkhauser-worlds-wound.reason: A still close figure and broad partition make a sparse composition. Selective facial light does not imply physical action, and the title is not treated as evidence of a viewer's psychology.

present.D: The face is selectively illuminated against a deeply shadowed hat, coat and background.
present.S: The vertical partition visibly separates the near plane from the figure in the recess.
present.F: The head and upper body dominate the close view.
present.P: The hat brim, facial contours, seams and clothing edges are controlled and distinct.
present.O: The broad, relatively uninterrupted partition leaves an open field alongside the figure.

unknown.N: The facial marks and partition may carry meanings, but visible secondary story clues cannot be confidently separated from the title and documentary context.
unknown.I: The archive describes a dream image, but this does not by itself establish a visibly impossible body or object.
unknown.X: Facial lines are accentuated; this reproduction does not make the difference between expressive alteration and conventionally rendered facial marks sufficiently clear.

req-rivera-controller-universe.alt: A worker operates a central machine between elliptical fields and many groups of people, plants and industrial forms.
req-rivera-controller-universe.note: The1934 Bellas Artes mural is preserved here as a complete institutional reproduction. It is the surviving Mexican version, not a photograph of the destroyed Rockefeller Center mural.
req-rivera-controller-universe.reason: People work, gesture and gather around a large mechanical centre. Numerous small incidents and repeated circles make it dense; literal environmental space is less dominant than the montage.

present.N: Workers, machinery, political crowds, plants and smaller activities supply many separate story clues.
present.I: Enlarged biological forms and incompatible scales occupy a visibly constructed, nonordinary montage.
present.G: Crossing elliptical fields, circular machinery and straight divisions strongly organise the composition.
present.V: People operate machinery, gesture and act within the surrounding groups.
present.X: Scale and the relative sizes of bodies and objects are conspicuously altered across the montage.
present.P: Faces, plant forms, machine fittings and small incidents have controlled edges.
present.R: Repeated circular parts, body groups and directional bands create a clear rhythm.
present.H: Hands, gazes and coordinated actions connect people within several groups.
present.T: A centrally presented operator is flanked by deliberately arranged opposing groups and displays.
present.M: Plant forms, mechanical parts, skin and clothing receive differentiated local descriptions.

req-rivera-alameda.alt: A long painted procession of people, trees and a dressed skeleton stretches across the museum wall, with visitors in front.
req-rivera-alameda.note: This photograph shows the complete mural in its museum setting. Real visitors partly obscure a few lower figures; they are not part of Rivera's painted scene.
req-rivera-alameda.reason: Many painted people stand, gesture and touch within a park-like setting. The crowd is dense but much of its bodily action is quiet; unpainted museum visitors are excluded from the content judgements.

present.N: Painted costumes, signs, objects, the skeleton and small encounters offer many clues beyond an individual pose.
present.I: A dressed skeleton stands among the painted people as an animate participant.
present.V: Several painted figures hold objects, reach and make emphatic hand gestures.
present.L: Substantial painted trees and park vegetation organise the upper setting.
present.X: Several painted faces and bodies are conspicuously caricatured or altered in proportion.
present.P: Painted faces, garments and small objects have controlled delineation.
present.R: Repeated upright figures, faces and hats form a long horizontal rhythm.
present.H: Painted figures hold hands, embrace and direct gazes toward one another.
present.M: Painted hats, garments, feathers and objects have differentiated local descriptions.

unknown.B: At the whole-mural photographic scale, distinct paint marks cannot be reliably separated from image texture or surface condition.

req-rivera-history-mexico.alt: A densely populated mural covers a curved stairway wall above a balustrade and museum visitors.
req-rivera-history-mexico.note: This is a central-wall section of the larger Epopeya del pueblo mexicano cycle. It is retained for gallery research, with no whole-cycle visual scores.
req-rivera-history-mexico.reason: Only one wall of a multiwall cycle is represented. Whole-cycle descriptors are unknown rather than inferred from this section.

req-siqueiros-new-democracy.alt: A large woman thrusts chained arms outward, with a torch, flower, fallen figures and forceful faces around her.
req-siqueiros-new-democracy.note: The complete central panel was painted in1944. The museum's Nueva democracia ensemble also includes two companion panels completed in1945.
req-siqueiros-new-democracy.reason: The thrusting arms and hands provide strong literal action. Bodies fill the field; the background supplies little environmental setting despite the dramatic effect.

present.N: Chains, torch, flower and fallen figures supply separate visible clues around the main action.
present.I: Oversized fists, heads and bodily scales form a physically uncanny montage rather than one ordinary encounter.
present.V: The central body thrusts its arms outward and several surrounding figures strain or reach.
present.F: A large near-view torso, hands and close bodily group occupy most of the panel.
present.X: Hands, faces and bodies are conspicuously enlarged and altered in proportion.
present.R: Repeated thrusting arms, rounded forms and sweeping directions organise the panel.
present.H: Bodies are visibly linked by force, restraint and directed gestures.
present.T: The central figure and flanking bodies are presented as a frontal staged encounter.

unknown.D: Bright and dark modelling is visible, but a selective illuminating source is less clear than the high chromatic contrast.
unknown.B: The institutional image does not reliably separate conspicuous paint marks from surface reproduction texture.
unknown.M: Large modelled forms are clear; fine material differentiation is unresolved at this source scale.

req-siqueiros-bourgeoisie.alt: A monochrome archive photograph shows workers and industrial forms in a foreshortened detail of a mural.
req-siqueiros-bourgeoisie.note: MIT identifies this as a left-wall detail photographed from an acute downward angle. It is not a full-colour or complete view of Retrato de la burguesía.
req-siqueiros-bourgeoisie.reason: This monochrome, oblique fragment cannot support whole-mural colour, composition or content assignments. All whole-work descriptors remain unknown.

req-siqueiros-march-humanity-section.alt: An interior section of a surrounding mural contains tall striped forms and a face-like motif, with lights reflecting above.
req-siqueiros-march-humanity-section.note: Only one interior section of La marcha de la humanidad is shown. The large surrounding mural and ceiling cannot be assessed from this view.
req-siqueiros-march-humanity-section.reason: A photographed section with glare is not a complete composition. Whole-mural descriptors remain unknown, and this view is excluded from ordinary study selection.

req-orozco-prometheus.alt: A large nude man raises both arms before red flame-like forms as clustered people reach and turn below him.
req-orozco-prometheus.note: Orozco painted this fresco for Frary Dining Hall in1930. The institutional source shows the complete main wall and its surrounding arch at native1100px width.
req-orozco-prometheus.reason: Emphatic reaching and turning bodies dominate the fresco. Fire-like fields and an arch surround them, but little natural or built setting is depicted within the painting.

present.N: The raised central body, clustered reactions and fire-like forms create several visible event clues.
present.I: The central body is visibly gigantic relative to the surrounding near figures, producing physically uncanny bodily scale.
present.D: Bright bodily planes are selected against deep dark areas and red fire-like surroundings.
present.V: The central figure reaches upward while surrounding people raise arms and turn.
present.F: A very large near-view torso and compact bodily groups occupy most of the painting.
present.X: The torso, arms and hands are elongated and enlarged in relation to surrounding bodies.
present.R: Repeated arms, body contours and rising flame-like streaks form a conspicuous directional rhythm.
present.H: Surrounding people direct coordinated attention and gestures toward the central action.

unknown.B: The native1100px image cannot reliably resolve separate paint marks across the full fresco.
unknown.P: Some contours are controlled, but the available whole-wall reproduction does not settle the fine-detail criterion.
unknown.M: The available source is insufficient for a confident judgement about fine depicted material surfaces.

req-orozco-man-fire.alt: An upward view shows a painted dome with a twisting red figure inside a circular field and surrounding radial panels.
req-orozco-man-fire.note: The institution dates the Cabañas fresco cycle1937–1939. This architectural photograph preserves the dome view rather than flattening it into an invented rectangular painting.
req-orozco-man-fire.reason: Painted bodies twist amid flame-like forms. The photographed ceiling architecture is distinct from depicted setting, and the small central figure does not become a close-up merely because it is monumental in person.

present.N: The central figure, surrounding bodies and radial painted scenes provide secondary clues.
present.I: Bodies appear suspended within a circular field of flame-like forms without a grounded physical setting.
present.G: Concentric and radial divisions visibly organise the painted dome and its framing fields.
present.V: The central body twists and stretches its limbs.
present.X: The central anatomy is conspicuously elongated and twisted.
present.R: Repeated radial compartments and circular bands form a strong visual rhythm.

unknown.D: Painted contrast and the illumination of the actual ceiling are difficult to separate in this photograph.
unknown.P: The distant dome photograph does not resolve fine contour and detail treatment confidently.
unknown.B: The camera distance does not resolve distinct paint marks.
unknown.H: Exchanges between the small painted bodies cannot be read confidently at this source scale.
unknown.M: Fine material description is unresolved at the photographed scale.

req-orozco-cortes-malinche.alt: Two seated figures occupy a fresco above a prone figure, with dark drapery and an agave-like plant below.
req-orozco-cortes-malinche.note: The complete fresco is photographed within its architectural setting. The lower prone figure is retained rather than silently cropping the image to the seated pair.
req-orozco-cortes-malinche.reason: The seated pair and lower body dominate a shallow pictorial space. An extended arm is visible, but the static pose is not scored as an active historical event.

present.N: The prone figure, extended arm and plant below provide clues beyond the seated pair.
present.V: The large extended forearm makes a conspicuous bodily gesture across the second seated figure.
present.F: The two near-view seated bodies dominate the fresco.
present.X: Angular torsos and altered bodily proportions conspicuously transform the anatomy.
present.P: Strong controlled contours define the limbs, torsos and faces.
present.H: Touch and the arm crossing the second figure visibly connect the seated pair.
present.T: A painted hanging drape frames the seated pair and lower body as a staged tableau.

unknown.B: The fresco surface and photographic exposure do not reliably identify distinct expressive paint marks.

req-orozco-katharsis.alt: Overlapping people, weapons and machines fill a mural with red, black and orange forms and a burning background.
req-orozco-katharsis.note: The complete mural is reproduced from the Bellas Artes museum guide. Its many bodily actions differ from a static posed group despite comparable human density.
req-orozco-katharsis.reason: Fighting, reaching and collapsing bodies supply strong literal action. Machines and bodies fill the field; flames contribute to the scene without making environmental setting dominant.

present.N: Weapons, machinery, fallen bodies and several separate encounters offer many event clues.
present.V: Bodies fight, strain, reach and fall across the mural.
present.F: Large near-view bodies and a compact foreground group occupy substantial pictorial space.
present.X: Faces, bodies and mechanical forms are conspicuously fragmented and altered in proportion.
present.B: Broken dark strokes and broad streaked modelling remain visible in faces and bodies.
present.R: Repeated barrel openings, mechanical shapes and curved bodies establish a directional rhythm.
present.H: Several bodies visibly confront, struggle with or act upon one another.

unknown.I: Some bodies and machines merge visually, but the boundary between expressive fragmentation and a literally impossible hybrid is unresolved.
unknown.D: The fiery palette and deep darks are clear, but selective illumination is difficult to distinguish from the colour organisation.

req-camarena-liberacion.alt: Angular figures and broken cross-like forms fill a red, green and purple mural, with a large back-facing body at the centre.
req-camarena-liberacion.note: The museum dates this mural1957–1963 and records acrylic on canvas. Sharp angular divisions offer a contrast with the sweeping bodies of the other new murals.
req-camarena-liberacion.reason: A central body breaks or strains against cross-like forms. Geometric planes divide the close figurative scene, while little environmental setting is depicted.

present.N: The cross-like forms, central action and differently treated flanking figures provide secondary clues.
present.G: Large angular planes and clearly divided colour fields strongly organise the image.
present.V: The central figure visibly strains and breaks away from cross-like forms.
present.F: Large near-view bodies occupy most of the mural.
present.X: Bodies and surrounding forms are conspicuously faceted and altered in proportion.
present.P: Sharp controlled boundaries separate the geometric planes and bodily contours.
present.R: Repeated angular directions and segmented planes establish a visible rhythm.
